The feature set and tech choices are conventional for an SSG and have many prior arts (Eleventy-like) that prove feasibility.

Biggest ways this could go wrong
- Missing site-wide build graph: If you treat it as a per-file transform instead of building a global content index first, tag pages and RSS will be incomplete or stale in watch mode.
- No base URL config: RSS and canonical links need absolute URLs; omitting this yields invalid feeds and broken links.
- Layouts in Handlebars: Core Handlebars lacks native layouts; you need a helper/plugin or a clear partials convention. Underestimating this adds brittle template glue.
- Dev-server injection coupling: Writing the live-reload script into files on disk risks leaking into production; better to inject at serve time only.

Evidence that would convince me the approach is wrong
- Correctness gaps in watch mode: a test where changing a post’s tags fails to update the affected tag index pages and RSS.
- RSS validation failures: a feed linter flags relative URLs, bad date formats, or invalid XML produced by Handlebars escaping rules.
- Layout friction: demonstrable inability to implement nested layouts or content blocks without third-party helpers, leading to convoluted templates or duplication.
- Performance regressions: benchmarks showing single-file edits trigger near full rebuilds (e.g., >1s for 1k pages) or memory spikes that don’t scale.
